caption: The drawing is composed of a rectangular area at the top with neatly handwritten text in Spanish, bordered by a dotted line. At the very top, there is a small cross-like symbol centered above the text. The main block of handwritten text takes up most of the upper half of the rectangle, written in brown ink. Below the text, within the rectangle, is a decorative horizontal band featuring a repeating grapevine motif, with clusters of grapes and leaves arranged symmetrically along the band. In each corner inside the border, similar small clusters of grapes and leaves are drawn. Extending below the rectangle and occupying much of the lower half of the page, there are several larger, branching grapevines. These vines are drawn in brown ink, with many bunches of grapes and small oval leaves sprouting from the branches, covering the area with a pattern of natural forms. The entire composition is rendered in a single shade of sepia or brown ink on a cream-colored background. There are no other colors present in the drawing.
title: Plate 3: Pecos Book of Visitations: From Portfolio "Spanish Colonial Designs of New Mexico"
